findings.title: retryCount-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new deleteMany uses an OR where the second branch is just `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table used by EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders too. Today only this SMS cron increments the counter, but any other code path (e.g. the email reminder cron adopting the same column, or a backfill) that raises retryCount above 1 on a non-SMS reminder will cause those reminders to be silently deleted by the SMS cron before they are ever sent. The retryCount clause should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to match the stated intent of the change.

findings.title: retryCount update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: Previously the catch block only logged the error, so a failure for one reminder could never stop the loop. Now the catch block performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update` unguarded. If that update itself fails — e.g. the row was deleted concurrently by another cron execution or by a booking cancellation, or the DB connection is the very thing that failed — the exception propagates out of the catch, the for-loop terminates, all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped for this run, and the handler returns a 500. The retry-count write in the catch should be wrapped in its own try/catch (or the loop should continue on failure) so one bad reminder cannot starve the rest.

findings.title: retryCount incremented via read-modify-write on a stale snapshot
findings.body: Both failure paths set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron executions overlap (possible when a run takes longer than the cron interval), both read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so a failure is not counted and deletion is delayed. Using Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids the lost update without changing the logic.

findings.title: No tests covering the new retry/delete behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces user-facing behavioral changes — reminders are deleted after two failed scheduling attempts, including via the catch-all error path — but adds no tests. There is nothing verifying that a reminder is deleted exactly after two failures (retryCount boundary `gt: 1`), that a reminder that fails once is retried and can still succeed, or that deterministic errors (e.g. template rendering throwing) also count toward deletion. A regression here silently drops customer SMS reminders, so at least the retry-count boundary and the delete query scope should be covered.
